title: TCP, UDP: Add fields for relative packet numbers within stream
description:
Add fields for relative packet numbers with TCP and UDP streams.

Move the UDP relative time calculation above the part where we
break out for zero payload.

Control the calculation with the same preferences that control
whether stream relative timestamps are calculated (presumably
users that want to turn one off would want to turn off the other.)

Fix #19250

added 14 commits
  • 904ccfc5...b42cd0df - 13 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • fa73289b - TCP, UDP: Add fields for relative packet numbers within stream
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/12597/diffs?diff_id=816752342&start_sha=904ccfc5187027a0fe9479908ed5c91a30497364)

I skimmed through the patch and have two questions:

* How does this work with out-of-order or duplicate packets?
* Are the numbers stable with two-pass dissection?

I am also surprised that `tcp.stream` is not mentioned in the WSUG. We have a whole section on [TCP Analysis](https://www.wireshark.org/docs/wsug_html_chunked/ChAdvTCPAnalysis.html), but nothing on that particular useful field. If that section would exist, then these new fields could also be documented there.

> How does this work with out-of-order or duplicate packets?

The number is incremented for each TCP or UDP header received in the order that they're in the packet (similar to the existing `frame.number`, the delta time calculations, or the proposed displayed number. For TCP, it's not "ordinal number in the stream according to TCP sequence number." Such a number would be difficult to compute, could only be done during desegmentation, and would be different depending on the preference settings for out-of-order processing and sequence number analysis. This should be stable.

Admittedly, the "ordinal number according to the TCP sequence number" is possibly useful, but it is a different request.

> Are the numbers stable with two-pass dissection?

Yes. The changes in two-pass dissection affect how dissectors under protocols that do reassembly work, but the number is incremented once for each TCP (or UDP) header, and even when other dissectors are called in different frames, TCP headers should be called in the same order. (A more precise caveat is that it might not be stable if there are other bugs, but it's not like the layer number issue that happens even without buggy behavior.)
